commit.message:
ccmain: set all results of ParagraphInfo and Orientation

PageIterator::ParagraphInfo() only set *just before it returned for a
paragraph without a model (e.g. on a page with a single line), so
is_list_item, is_crown and first_line_indent were not set, and
TessPageIteratorParagraphInfo() returned uninitialized values.

PageIterator::Orientation() did not set deskew_angle if there is no
block.

Set defaults for all results.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-O6ZIKBZD).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

wordstrbox: fix missing end of the last line of a page

GetWordStrBoxText() only wrote the end-of-line record and the newline
for the last text line if left, top, right and bottom of that line
were all non-zero. But 0 is a valid coordinate, so a last line which
touches the left or the top edge of the image was not terminated, and
the first record of the next page was appended to it.

Use the existing flag first_line, like GetLSTMBoxText() uses
first_word.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-62L14G1E).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

hocr: escape the language name and the document title

GetHOCRText() writes the input name, the font name and the recognized
text with HOcrEscape(), but not the language name in the lang
attribute of ocr_par and ocrx_word. That is the name under which the
model was loaded, so a quote or another markup character in the file
name of a traineddata gave broken or unwanted markup.

The same is true for the document title in the title element.

Escape both, and add unit tests.

The proposed test for the language name copied the model with
file::GetContents() and file::SetContents(), which truncate binary
data, so the model could not be loaded and the test was skipped. Copy
the file with std::filesystem, and fail if the model cannot be loaded.

Based on the fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner
(finding ANT-2026-IYB11TST).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

textord: skip the distance transform for blobs with a huge box

SetBlobStrokeWidth() clips the page to the bounding box of the blob
and runs pixDistanceFunction() and two scans over it, so the cost is
the area of the box, however small the blob is. A page with thin
nested rings or diagonal lines has hundreds of blobs with boxes of
nearly the size of the page, and the layout analysis took minutes.

Store zero widths if the area of the box is more than 128 times the
perimeter of the outline. Zero is what the function already stores
for a blob with not enough samples; users of the widths then use the
estimate from area and perimeter.

This changes the stroke widths of blobs like page-sized frames or scan
borders, of long thin lines and of very large glyphs.

The limit of 128 was tested with 237 pages of books, journals and
letters and with 101 pages of a newspaper (Deutscher Reichsanzeiger).
182 of these pages have blobs above the limit, mostly a single blob
which spans the whole page. For all pages of the first set and for
the 23 pages of the second set which have such blobs, the text and
hOCR output with model german_print2_15 and --psm 3 was identical
with and without this change, and the run time did not change
noticeably. A synthetic page of 2000 x 2000 pixels with nested rings
needs 4.3 s instead of 18.7 s.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-LZYJKPKM).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

textord: fix read out of bounds in GAPMAP for a map with one entry

With gapmap_no_isolated_quanta the test for an isolated quantum read
map[i + 1] for i == 0 and map[i - 1] for i == map_max without checking
whether these neighbours exist. For a block which is narrower than one
bucket (map_max == 0) both are outside of the array.

Only look at neighbours which exist. The result is the same for maps
with two or more entries. The single entry of a map with one entry is
now always handled as isolated.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-LETONEVL).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

textord: fix loop counters and a division by zero in GAPMAP

- The loops over the gap map counted with an int16_t and tested
  i <= map_max. For map_max == INT16_MAX (a block which is 32767
  pixels wide with a bucket size of 1) that test never fails: the
  counter wraps, and the loop writes in front of the map and does not
  end in builds with g++. Use int for the counters.

- The x-height of a row was narrowed to int16_t before it was added to
  the histogram. Values above 32767, which are possible with a large
  textord_min_xheight, became small or negative instead of being
  clipped to the range of the histogram by STATS::add(). That is how
  the bucket size got as small as 1 or 0.

- A median x-height below 2 gave a bucket size of 0 and a division by
  zero. Use a bucket size of at least 1.

The first two changes are the fix which was proposed by the scanner,
the third one was suggested by its review.

Based on the fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner
(finding ANT-2026-R518F4VZ).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

classify: avoid a float overflow in ReadParamDesc

Range and MidRange were calculated in float from the limits Min and
Max of a normproto file. For limits like -3e38 and 3e38 the difference
overflows, and the tesseract executable traps FE_OVERFLOW when it was
built with g++ (SIGFPE in Init()).

Calculate in double and clip the range to the range of float.

Add a unit test. ReadParamDesc() gets TESS_API for it, as the test
must also link with a shared library which hides its symbols.

Based on the fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner
(finding ANT-2026-0INCQPMJ).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

classify: avoid linear searches by unichar id in the adaptive matcher

With a shape table ExpandShapesAndApplyCorrections() searched
mapped_results for each unichar of each shape, AddNewResult() searched
the results for each new result, and ConvertMatchesToChoices() counted
the list of choices for each result. All of that is quadratic in the
size of a shape, so a model with a shape of thousands of unichars
needed minutes for a few words.

Use an index by unichar id for the first two searches and the existing
counter choices_length instead of the list length.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-MMH5CLWJ).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

cutil: fix null pointer dereference for the size of an empty LIST

An empty LIST is NIL_LIST (nullptr). Commit 2fa96b765 replaced the
function count(LIST) by the member function list_rec::size(). Calling
it for an empty list is undefined behaviour: clang removes the test
for a null pointer, and the code crashes. That happened in
PrintAdaptedTemplates() and in WriteAdaptedClass() for an adapted
class without temporary protos, for example at the end of a run with
classify_save_adapted_templates.

Restore the function count(), which handles an empty list.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-8AGHSUUG).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

classify: reject an inttemp class with too many protos

ReadIntTemplates() allocates ProtoLengths and ProtoSets[] from
NumProtoSets, but the adaption code (FindGoodProtos, AddIntProto)
indexes them by the proto id up to NumProtos. A file with NumProtos >
NumProtoSets * PROTOS_PER_PROTO_SET therefore caused accesses out of
bounds.

Add this condition to the existing check of the counts of a class.

Also avoid a division by a proto length of 0, which can come from a
file, too, in FindGoodProtos() and DisplayProtoDebugInfo().

Add unit tests.

Based on the fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner
(finding ANT-2026-5F5B0BAI).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

ccmain: fix read out of bounds in PrerecAllWordsPar for an empty word

PrerecAllWordsPar() (tessedit_parallelize) assumes that each ratings
matrix has a cell (0, 0). In LSTM-only mode a word without blobs is
not replaced by a fake word, so its ratings matrix has dimension 0,
and get(0, 0) read behind the empty array.

Skip such a word. It has no blobs which could be classified.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-XHAFVBQP).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

equationdetect: fix the comparators which are used for std::sort

SortCPByTopReverse(), SortCPByBottom() and SortCPByHeight() were
written for qsort: they get pointers to the elements and return an int
difference. Since commit 1f94d79c8 they are used with std::sort on a
std::vector<ColPartition *>, which passes the elements themselves and
expects a bool. Each function therefore used the first field of a
ColPartition as a pointer to a ColPartition and failed its own
ASSERT_HOST, so the page segmentation aborted whenever
textord_equation_detect was set and two text partitions had to be
sorted.

Take ColPartition pointers and return the result of a strict
comparison which gives the same order as before.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-ZGL3I80W).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

ccmain: do not abort on an unsupported tessedit_reject_mode

make_reject_map() only supports the values 0 and 5 for
tessedit_reject_mode and called ASSERT_HOST for any other value. That
aborted the process, also for users of the library, as soon as the
legacy engine recognized the first word.

Print a warning and use the default mode instead.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-W4VDS3BJ).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

wordrec: let same_point be true for equal points

The chopper relies on same_point() being true for two equal points:
near_point() uses it to refuse the insertion of a point which
coincides with the end of a segment. With chop_same_distance <= 0 the
test abs(0) < chop_same_distance fails, so vertical_projection_point()
inserted the same point again and again until the memory was used up.

Equal points are now the same for any value of chop_same_distance.
Nothing changes for values >= 1.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-MQFM0DHQ).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

textord: clip the ratio limits in compute_row_descdrop

compute_row_descdrop() converts row->xheight multiplied by
textord_ascx_ratio_min/max and textord_descx_ratio_min/max to int.
The conversion is undefined if the product is out of the int range,
which happens for a huge ratio from a config file. The loop which
counts the potential ascenders then ran over up to 2^31 indices for
each row.

Clip the ascender limits to the range of the histogram (they can only
narrow it) and the descender limits to +/-INT16_MAX before the
conversion. Nothing changes for values which were converted correctly
before.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-LSPRDZR1).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

textord: avoid divisions by zero for three integer parameters

textord_noise_sizefraction, edges_children_per_grandchild and
textord_spline_medianwin are used as divisors without any check, so a
value of 0 from a config file ended the process with SIGFPE.
textord_spline_medianwin is also used as the size of a median window,
and a value below 1 caused a read out of bounds in segment_baseline().

- clean_noise_from_row() and clean_noise_from_words() use the blob
  size as the threshold if textord_noise_sizefraction is not positive.
- OL_BUCKETS::count_children() counts no grandchildren if
  edges_children_per_grandchild is not positive.
- segment_baseline() falls back to a straight baseline if
  textord_spline_medianwin is not positive.

Nothing changes for positive values.

This is not a complete fix for all parameters: there are more
parameters which are used as divisors in floating point calculations
without a check.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-I7UIR1ID).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

textord: clamp textord_spline_medianwin in split_stepped_spline

split_stepped_spline() derives leftindex and rightindex from multiples
of textord_spline_medianwin and reads xcoords[leftindex - 1] and
xcoords[rightindex - 1]. The indices only stay inside
startindex..endindex if the window is at least 4. A smaller value
caused a read out of bounds, and a huge value overflowed the
multiplication by 3.

Use a local copy of the parameter which is clipped to [4, INT16_MAX].
The default value (6) is not affected.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-939MIPZ8).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

textord: do not chop an outline which is not left of the chop line

fixed_chop_coutline() walks the outline from its leftmost point, and
the walk only ends if that point is strictly left of the chop line.
The existing test left_edge >= chop_coord - pitch_error only
guarantees that for a pitch error which is not negative. The pitch
error is derived from the parameter textord_fp_chop_error, so a
negative value made the loop run forever.

Also test left_edge >= chop_coord. Nothing changes for parameter
values >= 0.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-RSH5HI6X).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

textord: clamp the trial pitch in compute_pitch_sd

compute_pitch_sd() fills the cells with a step of
static_cast<int16_t>(initial_pitch). check_pitch_sync() and
check_pitch_sync2() clamp their copy of the pitch to at least 3, but
the caller kept the raw value. With pitsync_linear_version 0 or 1 and
a large textord_pitch_range, tune_row_pitch() tries pitches below 1.
The step is 0 then, and the loop allocates cells until the memory is
used up.

Apply the same lower bound in compute_pitch_sd(). The default
(pitsync_linear_version 6) returns via compute_pitch_sd2() before the
clamp and is not changed.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-5CCTX4YZ).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

api: run the recognition if only the layout analysis was done

GetHOCRText(), GetAltoText(), GetPAGEText(), GetTSVText(),
GetLSTMBoxText() and GetWordStrBoxText() only called Recognize() if
page_res_ was null. After AnalyseLayout(), which is all that
ProcessPage() does for tessedit_pageseg_mode 2 (PSM_AUTO_ONLY),
page_res_ exists without recognition results, and the iterator
dereferenced a null pointer.

Test recognition_done_ like GetUTF8Text(), GetBoxText() and
GetUNLVText() do.

The PDF renderer uses the iterator directly and crashed in the same
way, so it gets the same test. It needs to be a friend class of
TessBaseAPI for that.

This change needs the fix for the state of recognition_done_ on empty
pages first (pull request #4528). Without that fix Recognize() does
not set recognition_done_ for an empty page, so each of these
functions would run the layout analysis of an empty page again.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-RBQXRM52).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

fontinfo: check the font ids before they are used as an index

FontInfoTable::SetContainsFontProperties() and
SetContainsMultipleFontProperties() used the font ids of the classifier
results as indices into the table without a check. In classifier_tester
the table is made from the font_properties file of the user, while the
ids come from the shape table of the model, so they need not match,
and the code read out of bounds.

Ignore ids which are not in the table, like
Tesseract::set_word_fonts() does.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-7OLQOJK3).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

training: fix crashes in AddSpacingInfo for a missing or bad xheight

MasterTrainer::AddSpacingInfo() divides by xheights_[fontinfo_id], but
xheights_ only gets its size from LoadXHeights(), which is only called
if the option -X was given, and LoadXHeights() accepted any integer.
Without -X the code read from an empty vector (SIGSEGV), and with an
x-height of 0 it divided by zero (SIGFPE).

Ignore the spacing file with a message if the font has no valid
x-height, like it is done for a file which matches no font. Also skip
x-heights which are not positive in LoadXHeights(), so such a font
gets the mean of the valid entries.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-TUPX5CXU).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

training: fix use after free in DeleteDeadSamples

TrainingSampleSet::DeleteDeadSamples() erased the entry of a dead
sample from the vector and then deleted *it. As erase() moves the
following entries down, that deleted the next (live) sample and left
a dangling pointer in the vector, while the dead sample was leaked.
shapeclustering and mftraining crashed.

Delete the sample first, and continue with the iterator which erase()
returns.

This was a regression from commit af131241a.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-6OZE8ZWP).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

lstm: reject weights which do not fit a float

With FAST_FLOAT (the default) WeightMatrix::DeSerialize() reads the
weights of a float matrix and the scales of an int matrix as double
and narrows them to float. A value beyond FLT_MAX, an infinity or a
NaN raises FE_OVERFLOW or FE_INVALID, which the tesseract executable
traps when it was built with g++ (SIGFPE in Init()).

Let the deserialization fail for such a value, as it does for other
corrupt matrices.

Add a unit test.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-QGN1GTJO).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

lstm: clip before converting to an integer in Tanh and Logistic

Tanh() and Logistic() scaled their argument and converted it to
unsigned before the index was compared with the size of the table.
The conversion of a value which does not fit is undefined: code built
with g++ raises FE_INVALID, which the tesseract executable traps
(SIGFPE), and a truncated index could pass the test, so the result was
far outside of the range of the function. The argument is only bounded
by the weights of the model.

Compare the argument with the saturation point before it is scaled.

NetworkIO::WriteTimeStepPart() had the same pattern (round to int,
then clip), so clip first there, too.

Add a unit test for both functions.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-7A38K5B7).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

matrix: keep the padding when a GENERIC_2D_ARRAY is copied

NetworkIO allocates its int8_t array with padding, because the SIMD
code for the matrix multiplication reads whole registers beyond the
last timestep. The copy assignment of GENERIC_2D_ARRAY resized the
destination without padding, so a copy (like *output = input in
Input::Forward()) could be read out of bounds by the following layer.

Remember the padding which was given to ResizeNoInit() and use it for
copies and moves.

Add a unit test.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-MZ7IPJ7U).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

lstm: limit the choices per timestep in SaveMostCertainChoices

The outputs of a softmax add up to 1, so at most 100 of them can reach
the threshold 0.01. A model whose last layer is not a softmax has no
such limit. The sorted insertion was quadratic in the number of
outputs then, and a list of all outputs was kept for each timestep.

Keep the 100 most likely choices. Their order is unchanged.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-SS02HWH1).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

lstm: zero the back deltas in Reconfig::Backward

Forward() truncates the output map, so input rows and columns which do
not fill a whole tile of x_scale by y_scale have no part in the
output. Backward() resizes back_deltas to the full input map without
initializing it and then only writes the positions of whole tiles. The
other positions kept old heap contents, which the layer below added to
its weights during training.

Zero the buffer after resizing it, as the Maxpool code does.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-T3JM0HM1).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

lstm: avoid a linear search in NetworkScratch::Stack::Return

Return() searched for the returned item from the top of the stack.
That is fast if the items are returned in reverse order, but a vector
of items is destroyed in the order in which they were borrowed, so
returning n items cost O(n^2). The 2-D LSTM borrows 2 * width items,
and its forward pass took minutes for a wide image.

Store the index of each item in a map and look it up.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-GSHSMLYD).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>

dawg: limit the number of positions in a DawgPositionVector

add_unique() searches the vector linearly, and nothing limited its
size. With dawgs which accept every string, the number of distinct
positions grows with the square of the word length, and the
recognition of a page took minutes.

Keep at most 256 positions. Real dictionaries only need a few.

Fix proposed by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-Q7Q3JVSG).

Assisted-by: OpenCode / Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Stefan Weil <sw@weilnetz.de>
